37720352.model_family: deep learning segmentation and classification model
37720352.body_region: brain (pediatric brain tumors: ependymoma, medulloblastoma, brainstem glioma, pilocytic astrocytoma)
37720352.clinical_problem: detecting and segmenting pediatric brain tumors on MRI and predicting tumor subtype from imaging features, to aid radiologists not trained in neuroradiology
37720352.patient_population: 94 cases (75 tumor cases across four tumor types, 19 normal MRI brain cases)
37720352.model_description: Deep learning automated segmentation and classification tool that segments pediatric brain tumors into whole, enhancing, and non-enhancing components on MRI and predicts tumor subtype from semantic MRI features, compared against radiologist assessment
37720352.headline_result: abnormality detection accuracy 90%, specificity 100%; tumor-type prediction accuracy near 80%; substantial agreement with radiologist (Cohen's kappa 0.695)
37720352.study_design: retrospective single-cohort study with training/test/validation split

37730747.model_family: machine learning brain-age prediction (morphometric similarity network versus cortical thickness/volume features)
37730747.clinical_problem: predicting brain age from structural MRI in healthy children and adolescents (6-17 years) using morphometric similarity network approaches, benchmarked against simpler single-feature models
37730747.patient_population: healthy children and adolescents aged 6-17 years from large-scale imaging databases
37730747.model_description: Machine learning Brainage prediction models comparing morphometric similarity mapping (a network-level structural MRI representation) against single-feature approaches (cortical thickness, cortical volume) for predicting chronological age from T1-weighted MRI in healthy children and adolescents
37730747.headline_result: morphometric similarity approaches did not outperform cortical thickness or cortical volume for age prediction; all models significantly biased by age but robust to motion confounds
37730747.study_design: benchmarking study of brain-age prediction methods in a healthy pediatric cohort

37738840.model_family: deep convolutional neural network with dilated residual connections and a fuzzy-c-means-inspired sift layer
37738840.clinical_problem: automatically estimating total brain volume from 3D cranial ultrasound in preterm infants to enable longitudinal monitoring of brain growth during NICU admission without manual segmentation
37738840.patient_population: preterm infants, imaged with two different ultrasound devices
37738840.model_description: Deep convolutional neural network (DSCNN) with dilated residual connections and a sift layer inspired by fuzzy c-means clustering that directly estimates total brain volume from 3D cranial ultrasound images in preterm infants without requiring image segmentation, benchmarked against AlexNet-3D, ResNet-3D, and VGG-3D
37738840.dataset_size: two datasets from two different ultrasound devices (size not specified)
37738840.headline_result: strong correlation between DSCNN predictions and observed total brain volume values, outperforming AlexNet-3D, ResNet-3D, and VGG-3D benchmarks
37738840.study_design: retrospective longitudinal model development and validation across two ultrasound devices

37747582.model_family: radiomics and deep learning AI models (automated segmentation and prediction)
37747582.body_region: neuroblastoma and diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
37747582.clinical_problem: how AI-derived imaging biomarkers and radiomics can noninvasively improve diagnosis and prognosis in pediatric neuroblastoma and diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
37747582.patient_population: pediatric oncology patients with neuroblastoma and diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
37747582.model_description: Review of the PRIMAGE European multi-center project, an open-cloud platform combining MRI, clinical, and molecular data with AI models (automated tumor detection/segmentation, radiomics and deep-feature extraction) to support personalized diagnosis and prognosis for pediatric neuroblastoma and diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
37747582.headline_result: automated tumor segmentation tool achieved a Dice similarity coefficient of 0.997 on an independent validation dataset
37747582.study_design: review describing a multi-center AI platform project (PRIMAGE)

37789758.clinical_problem: real-time evaluation of fetal ultrasound image quality and completeness of standard anatomical views, to assist inexperienced operators in fetal anomaly screening
37789758.patient_population: fetuses 18-32 weeks gestation, images from 2017-2018; validated on 836 videos (12,697 images) from four hospitals
37789758.model_description: YOLOv3-based deep learning system (PSAIS) with global (anatomic site) and local (structure) feature extraction that evaluates the quality of fetal ultrasound anatomical images in real time, recognizing 19 standard views and indicating existing or missing structures, validated against expert assessment
37789758.dataset_size: 134,696 training images; 836 validation videos (12,697 images) from four hospitals
37789758.headline_result: internal validation multiclass macro-average AUC 0.943 (95% CI 0.815-1.000); external validation AUC 0.958 (0.864-1.000); micro-average AUC 0.974/0.973; 90.9% accurate labeling of similar-to-standard views
37789758.study_design: retrospective multicenter development and external validation study

37993352.clinical_problem: predicting the risk of dilating vesicoureteral reflux in infants with antenatal hydronephrosis from early postnatal renal ultrasound findings, to better select candidates for voiding cystourethrogram
37993352.patient_population: 280 patients (540 renal units), infants aged 0-90 days at ultrasound, single institution
37993352.model_description: Machine learning model using ultrasound-derived Urinary Tract Dilation classification features (gender, ureteral dilation, parenchymal appearance, parenchymal thickness, central calyceal dilation) from early postnatal renal ultrasound to predict risk of dilating (grade 3 or higher) vesicoureteral reflux in infants with antenatal hydronephrosis
37993352.study_design: retrospective single-institution cohort study with train/test split

38043088.model_family: pyramid squeeze attention-guided dynamic multi-orientation feature fusion CNN (parallel weight-sharing Siamese network)
38043088.clinical_problem: predicting gestational age from fetal brain MRI to characterize normal brain development and aid diagnosis of congenital brain malformations, robust to fetal position variability and imbalanced imaging data
38043088.patient_population: 1,327 routine clinical T2-weighted MRI images from 157 subjects
38043088.model_description: Pyramid squeeze attention-guided dynamic multi-orientation feature fusion CNN (PDFF-CNN) with a balanced mean-squared-error loss, trained on an imbalanced fetal brain MRI dataset to robustly predict gestational age from T2-weighted images regardless of fetal position/orientation

38050002.model_family: machine learning classifiers (best: XGBoost-linear, random forest, among seven evaluated)
38050002.clinical_problem: automatically quantifying fetal brain gyrification from routinely acquired 2D MRI to detect gyrification abnormalities (lissencephaly, polymicrogyria)
38050002.patient_population: 162 fetuses from 2 clinical sites: 134 controls, 12 with lissencephaly, 13 with polymicrogyria, 3 suspected-but-normal
38050002.model_description: Automatic pipeline that segments the fetal brain on 2D T2-weighted MRI, computes five gyrification parameters per hemisphere, and applies machine learning classifiers (best-performing: XGBoost-linear, random forest) to differentiate lissencephaly and polymicrogyria from normal fetal brains
38050002.headline_result: XGBoost-linear AUC 0.90, recall 0.83 (lissencephaly vs control); random forest AUC 0.84, recall 0.62 (polymicrogyria vs control)

38074782.clinical_problem: automatically segmenting the neonatal lung on MRI and deriving 3D morphologic features to assess chronic lung disease (bronchopulmonary dysplasia) severity without radiation exposure
38074782.patient_population: two independent prospective cohorts of preterm infants (median gestational age 26.57 weeks), 86 with BPD and 21 without
38074782.model_description: CNN-based lung segmentation model for neonatal quiet-breathing MRI, combined with 3D reconstruction to compute lung volume, shape, pixel intensity, and surface features, correlated with lung injury scores and used to stratify bronchopulmonary dysplasia severity
38074782.headline_result: volumetric Dice 0.908 (cross-validation), 0.880 (independent test set); BPD vs no BPD AUC 0.92±0.02; mild vs moderate/severe BPD AUC 0.84±0.03
38074782.study_design: prospective two-cohort model development with independent test validation

38083430.model_family: transformer-based segmentation network (transfer learning) with a machine learning prediction model on radiomic features
38083430.clinical_problem: predicting future visual acuity loss in children with NF1-associated optic pathway glioma from multi-sequence MRI tumor size, shape, and imaging features, to inform early treatment decisions
38083430.patient_population: 75 pediatric subjects with NF1-associated optic pathway glioma (segmentation); a subset of 25 with ground-truth vision outcomes (prediction task)
38083430.model_description: Fully automatic framework combining a transformer-based transfer-learning segmentation network, statistical radiomic feature analysis, and a machine learning classifier to predict visual acuity loss in children with NF1-associated optic pathway glioma from multi-sequence MRI
38083430.headline_result: segmentation Dice similarity coefficient 0.791; vision-loss prediction accuracy 0.8 (cross-validation)

38088989.model_family: Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Recurrent Neural Network (Bi-LSTM-RNN) with reinforcement learning
38088989.clinical_problem: monitoring bladder fullness in children with nocturnal enuresis using a wearable ultrasound device to trigger a pre-void alarm and prevent bedwetting
38088989.patient_population: validation on a tissue-mimicking phantom and volunteers (ages not specified in abstract); intended clinical population is children with nocturnal enuresis
38088989.model_description: Wearable device (MyPAD) with bespoke miniaturized ultrasound probes and custom electronics that uses a Bi-LSTM-RNN with reinforcement learning to continuously monitor bladder fullness and trigger a pre-void alarm to prevent nocturnal enuresis in children
38088989.headline_result: sensitivity 99%, specificity 99.5%, overall accuracy 99.3% (phantom and volunteer validation)
38088989.study_design: early/pre-clinical engineering validation study on a phantom and volunteers

38109893.clinical_problem: detecting ileocolic intussusception on grayscale ultrasound images in children presenting for emergency ultrasonography
38109893.patient_population: 40,765 ultrasound images from children at two tertiary hospitals
38109893.model_description: Deep learning object-detection model that generates a bounding box with a confidence score to flag ileocolic intussusception on grayscale abdominal ultrasound images, trained/tuned/internally tested at one hospital and externally tested at a second hospital
38109893.headline_result: average precision 0.952 (internal test set), 0.936 (external test set); per-patient sensitivity 100.0%, specificity 97.1-99.0% depending on threshold
38109893.study_design: retrospective multicenter study with external test set

38222333.model_family: multimodal deep learning algorithm (SUV-guided candidate generation, location-aware classification, weighted multimodal feature fusion)
38222333.clinical_problem: automatically detecting pediatric lymphoma using combined PET and MRI imaging
38222333.patient_population: children (ages 0-19) with lymphoma imaged with simultaneous PET/MR
38222333.model_description: Multimodal deep learning algorithm combining standardized-uptake-value-guided tumor candidate generation, location-aware classification model learning, and weighted multimodal feature fusion of PET and MRI to automatically detect pediatric lymphoma, trained with limited data
38222333.headline_result: achieved superior tumor detection performance over state-of-the-art methods in their experiments (no single summary metric given)

38298774.model_family: nonlinear neural network models compared against linear models
38298774.clinical_problem: modeling how socioeconomic status, race, and experiences of discrimination relate to infant birth weight, gestational age, and brain volume, disentangling race as a proxy for structural factors
38298774.patient_population: 351 participants (birth weight/gestational age analysis); 280 participants with MRI scans (brain volume analysis)
38298774.model_description: Linear and nonlinear (neural network) models using demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical variables, including infant structural brain MRI volumes, to predict birth weight, gestational age, and brain development, comparing the relative importance of race versus socioeconomic factors
38298774.headline_result: nonlinear models better predicted birth weight than linear models (R2 0.172 vs 0.145, p=.005); race was not an important predictor of gestational age or brain volume

39935587.exclusion_reason: device landscape/cost review of portable ultrasound hardware; no AI/ML component described

35072752.model_family: deep learning segmentation model with transfer learning from adult scans
35072752.clinical_problem: automatically segmenting the claustrum in neonatal brain MRI, a structure linked to subplate neuron development affected by prematurity, using knowledge transferred from adult claustrum segmentation
35072752.patient_population: 558 T2-weighted neonatal brain MRIs from the developing Human Connectome Project; trained/evaluated on 30 manual annotations, applied to 528 scans
35072752.model_description: Deep learning-based claustrum segmentation model for T2-weighted neonatal brain MRI, using transfer learning from claustrum segmentation models trained on T1-weighted adult scans, requiring only a small number of neonatal annotations
35072752.release_evidence: The easy to use models and codes are made publicly available.
35072752.dataset_size: 558 neonatal MRIs (dHCP); trained on 30 manual annotations; applied to 528 scans
35072752.headline_result: median volumetric similarity 95.9%, robust Hausdorff distance 1.12 mm, Dice 80.0%; significantly superior to interrater reliability (p=0.047 volumetric similarity, p<0.005 Dice); reliable segmentation in 97.4% of 528 scans
35072752.study_design: retrospective model development with transfer learning, cross-validated

35200726.model_family: convolutional neural networks (segmentation and regression architectures)
35200726.clinical_problem: comparing segmentation-based versus direct regression-based deep learning approaches for estimating fetal head circumference from ultrasound images to monitor fetal growth
35200726.patient_population: public HC18 fetal head ultrasound dataset
35200726.model_description: Comparison of CNN segmentation-based (skull segmentation plus ellipse fitting) versus CNN regression-based (direct head-circumference estimation) approaches on the public HC18 fetal ultrasound dataset, evaluating accuracy, agreement, memory usage, and computational efficiency
35200726.headline_result: segmentation-based approaches delivered the most accurate results; regression CNNs produced promising but less accurate head-circumference estimates
35200726.study_design: retrospective comparative benchmarking study using a public dataset

35254181.exclusion_reason: ultrasound tongue biofeedback for speech therapy, not a radiologic diagnostic application

35463790.model_family: convolutional neural network (three-stage: view classification, segmentation/candidate detection, final inference)
35463790.clinical_problem: automatically detecting secundum atrial septal defect in children from color Doppler echocardiographic images across four standard views
35463790.patient_population: 4,031 training cases (370,057 images); independent test set of 229 cases (203,619 images: 105 with ASD, 124 with intact septum)
35463790.model_description: Three-stage fully automatic CNN-based system that identifies the four clinically relevant echocardiographic views, segments cardiac structures and detects ASD candidates, then infers a final ASD diagnosis from color Doppler echocardiograms in children
35463790.dataset_size: 4,031 training cases (370,057 images); independent test set of 229 cases (203,619 images)
35463790.headline_result: on independent test set: accuracy 0.8833, recall 0.8545, precision 0.8577, specificity 0.9136, F1 0.8546 (image-level averages across four views)
35463790.study_design: retrospective algorithm development with independent test set

35468204.exclusion_reason: fMRI study using conventional contrast/multivariate statistical analysis; no AI/ML model developed

35468984.model_family: Double Attention Res-U-Net (deep neural network with residual blocks and multi-scale attention gates)
35468984.body_region: multiple (colonoscopy polyps, multi-site MRI, and fetal ultrasound structures including crown-rump length and fetal foot)
35468984.clinical_problem: developing a general-purpose medical image segmentation architecture, evaluated in part on fetal biometry structures (crown-rump length, fetal foot) from ultrasound
35468984.patient_population: three datasets: CVC-ClinicDB colonoscopy images, a multi-site MRI dataset, and a collected fetal ultrasound dataset
35468984.model_description: Double Attention Res-U-Net, a novel deep neural network with residual blocks and multi-scale attention gates for medical image segmentation, evaluated on colonoscopy, multi-site MRI, and fetal ultrasound datasets (crown-rump length and fetal foot segmentation)
35468984.dataset_size: not specified for the fetal ultrasound dataset
35468984.headline_result: Dice/Jaccard 95.79%/91.62% for crown-rump length and 93.84%/89.08% for fetal foot segmentation; outperformed state-of-the-art U-Net-based models on external CVC-ClinicDB and multi-site MRI datasets
35468984.study_design: retrospective multi-dataset algorithm development and evaluation

35494868.model_family: generative adversarial network with residual dense connectivity (U-Net based)
35494868.body_region: multiple (lymph nodes, fetal head, brachial plexus)
35494868.clinical_problem: denoising ultrasound images (removing speckle noise) to improve image quality, evaluated in part on fetal head ultrasound
35494868.patient_population: Berkeley Segmentation Dataset with simulated speckle noise, plus clinical ultrasound images of lymph nodes, the fetal head, and the brachial plexus
35494868.model_description: Generative adversarial network with residual dense connectivity and a weighted joint loss (GAN-RW) for ultrasound image denoising, validated on simulated speckle-noise benchmarks and clinical ultrasound images including the fetal head
35494868.headline_result: GAN-RW improved PSNR by approximately 1.3-3.6% and SSIM by approximately 1.2-2.0% over existing denoising methods across noise levels 15/25/50; achieved the highest mean rank in the Friedman test
35494868.study_design: retrospective benchmark comparison against eight existing denoising algorithms

35578043.model_family: deep learning model adapted from a face-age estimation architecture
35578043.clinical_problem: estimating the age of birth-related clavicle fractures from infant radiographs, to help date skeletal injuries in suspected infant abuse investigations
35578043.patient_population: 416 clavicle radiographs from 213 infants aged 3 months or younger, single tertiary children's hospital, July 2003-March 2021
35578043.model_description: Deep learning model adapted from a face-age estimation architecture, trained to estimate the age of birth-related infant clavicle fractures from radiographs, evaluated by four-fold cross-validation as a potential virtual consultant for fracture dating in suspected abuse cases
35578043.headline_result: mean absolute error 4.2 days, RMSE 6.3 days, ICC 0.919; 83.7% of estimates accurate within 7 days of ground truth
35578043.study_design: retrospective single-center study with four-fold cross-validation

35788644.model_family: Neural Architecture Search (Learning by Teaching framework)
35788644.clinical_problem: automatically detecting pneumonia from chest X-rays, a disease with especially high pediatric mortality, using an automatically searched convolutional architecture
35788644.patient_population: pneumonia chest X-ray dataset with over 5,000 images
35788644.model_description: Neural Architecture Search method (Learning by Teaching framework) that automatically searches for the best convolutional architecture to detect pneumonia from chest X-rays
35788644.headline_result: AUC 97.6% for pneumonia detection, improving on previous NAS methods by 5.1 percentage points
35788644.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and benchmark comparison

35958478.model_family: deep learning CNN models (GoogleNet, VGG16/19, ResNet18/34/50) on CT radiomics
35958478.clinical_problem: differentiating otitis media caused by primary ciliary dyskinesia from simple otitis media with effusion in children using deep learning on temporal bone CT, to aid early diagnosis of primary ciliary dyskinesia
35958478.patient_population: 31 children with primary ciliary dyskinesia and 30 age-matched children with otitis media with effusion, single center
35958478.model_description: Deep learning CT radiomics models (GoogleNet, VGG16_bn, VGG19_bn, ResNet18, ResNet34, ResNet50) trained on temporal bone CT images to differentiate primary ciliary dyskinesia-related otitis media from simple otitis media with effusion in children

36207089.model_family: CNN-based pipeline (slice-selection modules and multi-view segmentation model)
36207089.body_region: neonatal brain (posterior limb of internal capsule)
36207089.clinical_problem: automatically segmenting the posterior limb of the internal capsule on MRI in preterm neonates, relevant for prognosis, replacing time-consuming manual segmentation
36207089.patient_population: preterm neonates; generalizability additionally tested on data from the developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP)
36207089.model_description: CNN-based pipeline with slice-selection modules and a multi-view segmentation model that identifies the relevant MRI slice and segments the posterior limb of the internal capsule in preterm neonates, evaluated against expert ratings and Dice score
36207089.headline_result: framework performance competitive with experts in accuracy (specific Dice score not given in abstract); generalizability confirmed on external dHCP data
36207089.study_design: retrospective model development with external dataset generalizability testing (dHCP)

36210944.exclusion_reason: acoustic/auscultation signal-based model (heart sounds from an electronic stethoscope), not diagnostic imaging

36287916.model_family: federated learning and traveling model (deep learning brain-age prediction)
36287916.clinical_problem: evaluating distributed machine learning approaches (federated learning versus the traveling model) for brain-age prediction from MRI when only small sample sizes are available per site, with stated relevance to pediatric and rare-disease research
36287916.patient_population: 2,025 T1-weighted MRI scans, distributed learning scenarios simulated across multiple sites
36287916.model_description: Deep learning brain-age prediction models trained using federated learning (parallel local training with aggregation) versus the traveling model (sequential site-to-site training), compared across 18 scenarios of sample size per site and training rounds
36287916.headline_result: traveling model outperformed federated learning at every sample size tested; with 1 sample per site, federated learning MAE 18.9±0.13 years versus traveling model MAE 6.21±0.50 years, comparable to central learning MAE 5.99 years
36287916.study_design: simulation study comparing distributed learning strategies across multiple sample-size scenarios

36302858.exclusion_reason: review of AI/ML for predicting chemotherapy-related complications in pediatric oncology; imaging AI mentioned only in passing as broader context, not the review's focus

36517850.model_family: deep learning (UNETR) and atlas-guided registration for automated multi-label segmentation
36517850.clinical_problem: creating population-averaged 3D atlases of normal and abnormal fetal cardiovascular anatomy and automating multi-label segmentation of fetal cardiac vessels using deep learning
36517850.patient_population: 86 third-trimester fetuses (29-34 weeks gestation): 28 healthy controls, 20 with coarctation of the aorta, 38 with vascular rings (21 right aortic arch, 17 double aortic arch)
36517850.model_description: Deep learning (UNETR transformer-based segmentation network) and atlas-guided registration methods for automated 3D multi-label segmentation of fetal cardiac vessels on black-blood T2-weighted fetal cardiovascular MRI, used to build population-averaged atlases of normal and abnormal fetal aortic arch anatomy
36517850.dataset_size: 86 fetuses total; 42 used for training, 3 for validation, 6 for testing
36517850.headline_result: 100% per-vessel detection rate for both normal and abnormal aortic arch anatomy
36517850.study_design: retrospective atlas construction and deep learning segmentation development study

36538911.clinical_problem: quantifying complex 3D fetal limb motion in utero from BOLD MRI to assess maternal, placental, and fetal factors affecting fetal movement as a potential biomarker of fetal health and neuromuscular development
36538911.patient_population: 76 sets of fetal (24-40 gestational weeks) BOLD MRI scans from 52 pregnant women (18-45 years old)
36538911.model_description: 3D convolutional neural network previously trained to track fetal key points (wrists, elbows, shoulders, ankles, knees, hips) on BOLD MRI time series, used to quantify upper and lower limb kinematics and absolute movement time across gestation and under maternal hyperoxia
36538911.dataset_size: 76 fetal MRI scan sets from 52 women
36538911.headline_result: significantly longer limb movement duration during maternal hyperoxia; centrifugal increase in movement across limbs; longer upper-extremity movement before 31 gestational weeks and lower-extremity movement after 35 gestational weeks

36572942.model_family: deep convolutional neural networks (two CNNs: liver segmentation, trauma segmentation)
36572942.clinical_problem: automated quantitative assessment of pediatric blunt hepatic trauma severity from contrast-enhanced CT, to supplement current AAST grading
36572942.patient_population: 170 children with blunt hepatic trauma, May 2015-August 2021, single center
36572942.model_description: End-to-end deep learning framework using two CNNs to segment liver parenchyma and liver trauma regions on contrast-enhanced CT, automatically computing liver volume, trauma volume, and the liver parenchymal disruption index to grade pediatric blunt hepatic trauma severity
36572942.headline_result: liver segmentation Dice 94.75%; trauma segmentation Dice 72.91%; liver parenchymal disruption index and trauma volume correlated with AAST grade (rho 0.823/0.831, p<0.001); AUC 0.942 (LPDI) and 0.952 (trauma volume) for distinguishing high- versus low-grade trauma
36572942.study_design: retrospective single-center study with temporal train/test split

36574278.exclusion_reason: qualitative acceptability/feasibility study of stakeholder perceptions of an AI-enabled device; does not evaluate the AI model's diagnostic performance

36620600.exclusion_reason: radiomic/imaging deformation feature analysis using conventional statistical association testing (ANOVA, Kaplan-Meier); no machine learning classifier built
